messages.content:
The writer's note about it, in their words: A comment in a fan theory thread in r/WarriorCats. Fans like evidence from the books, and a little humour.
A learner of English is rewriting part of a post for Reddit (r/WarriorCats):
<<<
I don't think it is not StarClan's fault. When the Clans at the Moonstone and the sky is overcast, so the moonlight cannot reach the stone, maybe the clouds alone explain it?

* * *

No no, I mean StarClan didn't abandon them on purpose. They wanted to come, but without moonlight the Moonstone can't work, so they can't reach the cats.
>>>
The part: "When the Clans at the Moonstone and the sky is overcast, so the moonlight cannot reach the stone, maybe the clouds alone explain it?"
What is wrong with it: 1. It has no clear referent, and "alone" makes the clouds the only cause, which a reader takes as ruling out StarClan altogether. That is what made frostkit ask whether StarClan is real.
2. The sentence still stacks a condition, a cause and a guess, and the "so" introduces the cause before the guess arrives at "maybe", so the chain is hard to follow. An English reader expects a "so" to lead straight to the conclusion.
What they mean (confirmed by them): 1. the clouds explain why StarClan has been silent
2. Everything this passage says now: every point, question, hedge and feeling in it stays; only how it is put changes.
A version that works (never show it or any stretch of it): "Maybe the clouds are the reason StarClan has gone quiet? When the Clans meet at the Moonstone under an overcast sky, the moonlight can't reach the stone."
Words they already have as hints: cloud cover, overcast
They are stuck. Write two hints that help them build it themselves, never giving them the wording:
- plan: in English, one or two short sentences, as their tutor: how a fluent writer builds this part: what comes first, what follows, how the parts connect (contrast, cause, addition) and where the emphasis goes. Name no English word except the hint words above (none from the working version), no letter counts, no fill-in blanks. It is about the words of this part, never the content they talk about ("first the interactions between them, then…" plans a story, not the sentence). When the part is a word or two (left in Simplified Chinese (as used in mainland China), or a missing word), say what kind of word goes there and how it sits in the sentence.
- example: one short English sentence a fluent writer would actually write (grammatical and natural on its own), about an everyday topic unrelated to the post (different people, things and events), built the same way as the working version: the same pattern and the same connecting words, none of its other content words. Put [square brackets] around the few words it shares with the working version as they are (the frame they can borrow, at most four), never around the words that change.
The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in English.
Reply with JSON only: {"plan":"","example":""}

result.text: {"plan":"Open with the guess as a short question, since that is the point the writer is really raising. Then begin a second sentence that sets the scene with a clause about when the meeting happens, followed by the main clause, and let the emphasis fall on what the moonlight cannot do at the end.","example":"[When] my brother reaches [the] station [under] heavy rain, he [can't] find his ticket."}
